0.long_answer: The autosomal dominant form of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is associated with mutations in several genes. When focusing on the gene located on chromosome 1, the relevant gene is COL9A2. Among the genes known to cause the dominant form of the disorder, COMP is on chromosome 19, COL9A1 is on chromosome 6, COL9A2 is on chromosome 1, COL9A3 is on chromosome 20, and MATN3 is on chromosome 2. Therefore, the gene on chromosome 1 responsible for the autosomal dominant form is COL9A2.
